notes: Arduino Due, Arduino Motor Shield and wall wart supply are not in the catalogue, so they are new part types; only the ports used are meaningful for the shield (pins 3 PWM_A, 12 DIR_A, 9 BRAKE_A, A0 SNS_A).

The motor's two wires are permanently attached to the motor, so motor ports 1/2 connect straight to the shield's channel A screw terminals (red to +, black to -, as in the photo); no jumper wires are used.

The shield is stacked on the Due so every shield header pin is joined to the matching Due socket; only the pins the sketch uses plus power pins are listed. The shield's VIN header pin carries the 12V from the Due's VIN to the shield's motor driver; this is a real power feed from the stacked header, not a direct pin-to-pin shortcut.
The shield's separate VIN/GND screw terminals are not used by this tutorial (power comes through the Due's DC jack), so they were removed from the shield part to avoid an unwired internal link.

Wall wart (12V used with the fan) plugs into the Due DC jack, modelled as a header-socket so the wire-end plug is a compatible join; its mains plug is not modelled. The DC- side is internal to the barrel jack, so only DC+ is wired to DC-JACK.
The USB cable goes to the Due programming port (USB-PROG) and to the computer; the photo shows both USB and power cables attached.
